clue.text: The best tool — it breaks

definitions.meaning: the choice or finest of a group
a pointed implement for breaking up hard ground or ice

explanation.definitionFit: The finest of a selection is called its choice one, and a pointed digging implement for breaking ground shares the same name.

clue.text: Carry out golf shot — hard on grass bordering fairway

parts.note: a putt is a short golf stroke on the green
H is the standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the rough is the longer grass alongside a golf fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a shot from the long grass at the edge of the fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a plan or deal through to completion is to accomplish or execute it.

clue.text: Care for amusing person

definitions.meaning: informally, a funny or outrageous character, as in 'he's a real ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Wariness is a synonym of care, and colloquially a comic, entertaining character is called by the same word.

clue.text: A way to relax includes excursion to see adult show

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, so the word for excursion sits within the way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a trip is an outing or excursion
to ease is to loosen or relax

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a holiday outing as a way to unwind, ending up at a show for grown-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance in which a dancer gradually undresses is a classic adults-only entertainment.

clue.text: Securing outside parts of theatre before musical drama

indicators.note: the outermost letters, first and last, of the word theatre are taken

parts.note: The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four music dramas, Der Ring des Nibelungen

explanation.surface: Something at the edges of a theatre happens before an opera begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' places TE ahead of THE RING; Wagner's operatic cycle is popularly called The Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying an animal or object down with a rope is fastening or securing it.

clue.text: Plain diagram shows this vast country

indicators.note: the clue words display the answer within them, running across the two words plain and diagram

explanation.surface: A simple chart depicts an enormous nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The subcontinental republic is among the largest nations on Earth by area and population.

clue.text: Hut's repairers rebuilt office for financial manager

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word with its S kept

explanation.surface: Builders who mend a shed reconstruct it into an office for a money manager.
explanation.definitionFit: The post held by someone in charge of an organisation's funds is that role or office.

clue.text: A lawyer with gammy leg goes for a walk in America

indicators.note: here the leg word is put in with, that is placed inside, the lawyer pair

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
gammy is British slang for injured or lame

explanation.surface: An American attorney with a bad leg sets off for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' signals insertion here: the bad leg is set inside the lawyer pair. GAMMY is informal British for crippled or injured; DA is the American District Attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American Southwest, a tree-lined public promenade or walkway is given this Spanish-derived name.

clue.text: Religious American lady in a whirl

definitions.meaning: Mary Baker ... founded the Christian Science church
a swirling current of water or air

explanation.definitionFit: The founder of Christian Science bore this surname, and a small whirlpool or swirling current has the same name.

clue.text: The last thing a Christian expects to hear?

definitions.text: The last thing a Christian expects to hear?

parts.words: The last thing a Christian expects to hear?
parts.note: the Last Trump sounded on Judgement Day, read as the final sound a believer awaits, with a play on 'the last thing you'd expect'

explanation.definitionFit: Christian tradition holds that a brass instrument's blast, the Last Trump, will herald the end of the world.

clue.text: Old coins — two reasonably circular shapes?

definitions.meaning: Spanish silver dollars worth eight reales, famous from pirate tales
the numeral 8 drawn as two roughly round loops, so the bits that make up an eight

explanation.definitionFit: Spanish dollars were valued at eight reales, and the figure 8 is made of two roughly circular parts.

clue.text: Conservative hid with a Red on the rampage

indicators.note: running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory hid while a Communist ran riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rampage' scrambles HID and A RED together.
explanation.definitionFit: A diehard is a stubborn traditionalist resisting change, which suits a staunch conservative.

clue.text: Emperor wants Sheila, scatty English girl

indicators.note: scatty means scatterbrained and disorganised, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a lassie is a Scottish word for a girl

explanation.surface: A ruler desires a scatterbrained English girl called Sheila.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the last Emperor of Ethiopia, reigning until 1974.

clue.text: Rocket engineer walks over, embracing female

indicators.note: one piece hugs another, so the word for a female bird goes inside

parts.note: to step on something is to walk over it
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: An engineer strides across, hugging a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stephenson built the famous early locomotive called the Rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The railway pioneer George Stephenson designed the Rocket locomotive in 1829.

clue.text: Cat is one of a number in the pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asian mountains

definitions.text: one of a number in the pound
definitions.meaning: a pound weight is made up of sixteen of these units

explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also known by this name, and sixteen of these weight units make up a pound.

clue.text: It's vital to bring in a worker

parts.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
an ant is the classic worker insect in crosswords

explanation.surface: A businessman says it is essential to bring in another employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial or essential is of great significance, a near synonym of vital.

clue.text: Plane in US crashed in strip of land

indicators.note: a crashed aircraft is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: An aircraft came down in America on a narrow tract of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition, while the first is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is a projection of land almost surrounded by water, often long and narrow.

clue.text: Old county's very attractive little publication

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just old county

parts.note: glam is a shortened form of glamorous, very attractive
an organ is a newspaper or periodical serving a group

explanation.surface: A former shire's magazine is small but stunningly pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: This was a historic county of South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a historic county in South Wales, abolished in local government reorganisation in 1974.

clue.text: On island all conifers initially grow together

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the words all and conifers is taken

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: Every pine tree on a Mediterranean island starts to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places AC above CRETE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by gradual accumulation, things building up together into one mass.

clue.text: Course at university needs preparatory period

parts.note: a run is a course or route
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A course of study at college requires some time to get ready first.
explanation.definitionFit: The time leading up to an event, spent getting ready, is commonly called this.

clue.text: Grey trying to keep out of the war

definitions.meaning: a colourless, drab shade such as beige or grey

definitions.text: trying to keep out of the war
definitions.meaning: taking no side in a conflict, like Switzerland

explanation.definitionFit: Beige and grey are colourless shades of this kind, and a nation staying out of a conflict takes the same stance.

clue.text: Financial agency preparing to move to another building?

definitions.meaning: a central office settling transactions between banks

definitions.text: preparing to move to another building?
definitions.meaning: emptying out one's home before relocating

explanation.definitionFit: A bank office settling cheques bears this name, and emptying a dwelling before moving out is the punning sense.

clue.text: Part of mountain trip involving scrambling at the end?

indicators.note: one piece takes in another, so the final letter is placed inside the trip word

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

indicators.note: the last letter of the word scrambling is taken

explanation.surface: A mountain journey ends with a bit of a scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow crest running along the top of a mountain is called by this name.

clue.text: Brandy used as currency once, it's said

indicators.note: a spoken version of the word for an old currency is meant

parts.note: the mark was the former German currency, replaced by the euro

explanation.surface: Someone claims a spirit was once used as money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' gives a word sounding like MARK; 'used as' joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a French brandy distilled from grape skins and pips left after pressing.

clue.text: Notice about day of victory involving English being paid back

indicators.note: the notice word goes around everything else

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or notice

indicators.note: the victory letters take in the abbreviation for English

parts.note: VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: A notice marking VE Day with English involvement says a debt is being settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' builds VENGE; 'about' wraps the notice round it. VE Day marked Allied victory in Europe in 1945. 'being' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to repay it with retaliation, so a wrong revenged has been paid back.

clue.text: Upper-class politicians admitting anger —- they want fair play

indicators.note: letting something in, so the anger word goes inside the politicians

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Posh Members of Parliament let their tempers show while demanding fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports officials who enforce the rules are those who insist on fair play.

clue.text: Jack Sprat wouldn't gossip

definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme says Jack Sprat could eat no fat, so he would not munch it
an informal phrase for chatting idly at length

explanation.definitionFit: Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme refused fatty food, and the same phrase is slang for idle chatting.

clue.text: Not finishing side dish

indicators.note: the side word loses its final letter

parts.note: a flank is a side, of a body or an army

explanation.surface: An unfinished side dish sits on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not finishing' cuts the K from FLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry or sponge case with a filling, a sweet or savoury dish.
